# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration cand_0002 (2/3). Parent cand_0001 scored val 0.600 (24/40 pass).

Evidence:
- The cand_0001 val traces in `trajectories/`, dumped to text.
- An init-vs-golden diff over answer_position for all 16 failing tasks. Golden files were used only to name the CLASS of error; no value from them is in the edit.
- A per-task count of prefilled, changed and formula cells inside answer_position for all 40 tasks.
- The scorer (`evaluation.py`): `transform_value` / `compare_cell_value`.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | leverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A: formula cells already in answer_position | 183-8, 524-31, 45944 (also 1925 partly) | The agent rewrote only the cells it meant to change and left the existing formula cells as formulas. openpyxl drops their cached value, so they read back empty. 183-8: row 7 SUM/AVERAGE have cached #DIV/0!; the instruction says "only J3:L6", but I3:L7 is graded. The parent's feedback says so directly: "answer cells hold FORMULAS". | KNOWLEDGE (grader) + BEHAVIORAL (no check) | 3 tasks, mechanical |
| 2 | B: exact text from workbook strings and formula constants | 1925 ("NEW" constant in the existing IFNA formula vs the instruction's "New"), 203-15 (header plurals) | The §1(b) rule existed and was skipped, so the fix has to be STRUCTURE: a verify-phase check. | BEHAVIORAL | 2 |
| 3 | C: sample-output sheet | 409-45 (desired result keeps blank separator rows), 534-26 (the Result sheet's 2020 cutoff copied instead of today) | No rule said how to use an Expected/Result sheet. It was over-trusted for data-dependent cutoffs and under-used for layout. | KNOWLEDGE | 2 (534-26 was a cand_0001 break) |
| 4 | D: instruction-stated example not calibrated | 50521 (the instruction says customer 1 → 5; the agent wrote 2) | Phase 1 calibrated only against a filled sibling column, not against a value stated in the prose. | BEHAVIORAL | 1 (a cand_0001 break) |
| 5 | I: computing from the formula workbook | 45707 (30 rounds, empty output) | The A column is `=A2+1`. The agent computed from the non-data_only workbook, so the dates were strings and every check missed. | KNOWLEDGE | 1 |
| 6 | F: header defines content | 188-39 (a cand_0001 break; the Designation column got the name) | Prose "list the name" was followed over the target header. | KNOWLEDGE | 1 |
| 7 | G: named subset | 12307 (counted every country column, not just the Table-1 list) | The instruction's subset was ignored. | KNOWLEDGE | 1 |
| 8 | E: prefilled cells changed | 57354 (B3/C3 prefilled; the golden keeps them) | The rule exists and was skipped, so it becomes a verify check. | BEHAVIORAL | 1 |
| — | rest | 290-1 (6 distinct blocks in 30 turns; the golden continues the K..U pattern beyond rows 2-3), 58687, 59129, 279-23 | Distinct logic errors, no shared mechanism | CAPABILITY | skipped |

## Changes made this iteration
| # | cluster | lever | file | what |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | A | tighten the output contract + add the reason | task_template.md CONTRACT 1 | Existing formula cells in answer_position must be overwritten with literals: the cached value, or a recomputed value when the cache is an error or depends on changed cells. This holds even when the instruction names a narrower range. |
| E2 | A | restructure (check in readback) | task_template.md Phase 2 code + Phase 3 first bullet | Reload the output WITHOUT data_only and print `formula cells left`; Phase 3 requires the list to be empty. |
| E3 | I | add the reason | task_template.md Phase 1 | Compute from `ws` (data_only). `wsf` returns formula text, e.g. `'=A2+1'` instead of a date. |
| E4 | D | restructure (ordered calibration list) | task_template.md Phase 1 | Calibrate against an expected result the instruction states, as well as against a sibling column; print it beside the stated value. |
| E5 | B | restructure (verify check) | task_template.md Phase 3 | Text matching a workbook string or a formula's quoted constant apart from case, spacing or plural → use the exact workbook spelling. |
| E6 | E | rewrite positively (verify check) | task_template.md Phase 3 | Each target cell that changed from `was:` must be one the instruction asks to change; otherwise restore it. |
| E7 | C | add a sourced rule | prompt.md §2 | A sample-output sheet specifies the layout (surviving rows, separator blanks, column order, header text). Data-dependent cutoffs are recomputed from the instruction and today. If answer_position is on that sheet, its filled cells are kept. |
| E8 | F | add an example | prompt.md §2 headers | A target column's header says what goes in it. The example uses a generic `Department` header, not the task's own. |
| E9 | G | add a sourced rule | prompt.md §2 | An instruction-named subset: collect it, print it, and aggregate over its members only. |

## Verify-the-fix
- E1/E2 → 183-8 has formulas in I3:I6 and I7:L7. The readback lists them, so the agent must write I3:I6 from the cache and recompute row 7 from its own J:L values (golden row 7 equals the SUM/AVERAGE of rows 3-6). 524-31 / 45944 have error caches, which must be recomputed.
- E1/E2 safety → I listed the protected tasks that have formula targets (11276, 52541, 56921). All three were passed by writing literals, so the check prints an empty list and nothing changes. 52541: 4/5 golden values equal the cache, so writing the cache is right there too. No protected task has a formula target whose golden value is empty.
- E3 → 45707: A3:A69 are `=A{r-1}+1`, and the data_only cache holds datetimes (I checked: A33 = 2000-02-01). With `ws`, the next-day check finds rows 32 and 61, which matches the golden D32=5 and D61=4.
- E4 → 50521: the instruction states customer 1 = 5. The agent's N4 was 2, and printing that beside 5 forces a re-read. On protected tasks the check applies only when the prose states a value.
- E5 → 1925: the formula constant is "NEW" (golden C6/C7 = 'NEW'). 203-15: header plurals. Safety: a script over all 24 protected tasks found no golden text in answer_position that differs from a workbook string only by case or spacing. The check therefore cannot push any of them to a different spelling.
- E6 → 57354: B3/C3 were prefilled, and the golden keeps them.
- E7 → 409-45 keeps the desired-result blank separators. 534-26: the rule explicitly says the sample's cutoff is not the threshold for "current", which fixes the parent's break (its trace says "the 'Result' sheet is a hint… the threshold is 2020-12"). Protected 547-43 has answer_position ON the Expected sheet with 72 prefilled cells that are all unchanged in the golden; the last sentence keeps them. Protected 48975 (an Output sheet, not an example) is unaffected.
- E8 → 188-39: the golden's B column = designation under the 'Designation' header. A generic example was used so no answer is hardcoded.
- E9 → 12307: the golden is 2/2 (the Table-1 subset); the agent wrote 5/3 (all columns).
- Blast radius: every §2 rule (E7-E9) is gated on a visible situation: a sample sheet exists, a header conflicts with the prose, or the prose names a subset. The template checks (E2, E5, E6) only print or compare and change nothing when the answer is already right. Placeholders were verified with `str.format` on the comment-stripped template.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features: none. The session rules say not to call Agent or workflows unless the user requests it, so I worked serially.
- Prior iterations read: prior_iterations/cand_0001/PROCESS.md and LEDGER.md. Its breaks (188-39, 50521, 534-26) are targeted directly by E8, E4 and E7. Nothing from cand_0001 was removed.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- Everything in cand_0001: the literal contract, keep-type, keep-originals, delete = shift, the today rule, and the explicit stop.
- The formula-cells-left readback (E2): it is the cheapest detector of the most mechanical failure class.

## Deliberately skipped
- 290-1: a pattern-continuation logic error (the agent spent 30 rounds on 6 distinct blocks). A pattern rule would be task-specific.
- 58687, 59129, 279-23: distinct logic errors with no shared mechanism. 279-23 (extract inside delimiters) is too narrow for one task.
- No edit to the adapter, harness or scorer, and no evaluation run.
